name: sap-cdp
_readme: SAP Customer Data Platform (SAP CDP) as a TARGET pack for tech-fit estimation of brownfield extensions (a client runs CDP in one market and adds a country / business unit) and as the standard critic's knowledge (standard-sap-cdp). Generic product knowledge only - no client content. Built 2026-10-05 from the help.sap.com content service (all CDP deliverables crawled and quote-checked) plus the Commerce-side connector modules under SAP_COMMERCE_INTEGRATIONS; no adapter.py (no code scanning). Verified facts: reference-cache.md; open items: research-seed.md.

as_target.default_frontend: no customer-facing frontend - administration console (Universe); activation through destination applications

snippets.critic2_persona: seasoned SAP Customer Data Platform solution architect who has set up and extended multi-business-unit CDP tenants (Legacy and SAP Integrated business units, B2B groups and relationships, business areas) and integrated them with SAP Commerce Cloud, SAP Customer Data Cloud, SAP Emarsys / SAP Engagement Cloud and SAP S/4HANA via SAP Cloud Integration; knows the published limits by heart and challenges every 'standard' or 'just configuration' claim: which connector (current or Legacy), which direction, which event or action, which business-unit variant and which documented limit it depends on, and what still has to be built or re-created per business unit
snippets.docs_domains: help.sap.com product SAP_CUSTOMER_DATA_PLATFORM - deliverables User Guide (8438f051ded544d2ba1303e67fc5ff86), Integration Guide (8b7bed724cb94ae68065fdac8c4350db), APIs (0bcecc2a324f49e288b8026bbcd7a0da), What's New Viewer (06a1655d021b4100b30991608bc2b554), Onboarding Guide (96355585039443758f89a9e6c7c81298), Security Guide (17b75b9ee51d44d89b7aa006e6a41e60); the Commerce side of the connectors lives under SAP_COMMERCE_INTEGRATIONS (SAP One Domain Model Integration e1131537fd3a43a6b600feddfbae7ab8, SAP Personalization Connectivity f66be0d6fd55499796031f69c6822263). help.sap.com is a JS application that answers HTTP 200 for any URL and WebFetch cannot read it: verify a topic with `python3 <plugin>/knowledge/platforms/sap-commerce/tools/saphelp.py <topic-url>` (deliverableMetadata + pagecontent) and search with `python3 <plugin>/knowledge/platforms/sap-commerce/tools/sapsearch.py "<query>" SAP_CUSTOMER_DATA_PLATFORM`. Further: api.sap.com (SAP Business Accelerator Hub: Cloud Integration package 'SAP S/4HANA Integration with SAP Customer Data Platform'), sap.com product pages (positioning only), SAP for Me (provisioning, entitlements). The product has no version numbers - it is a continuously delivered cloud service: date every fact.
snippets.best_practice: Configure before you build: schema attributes, matching and merge rules, purposes, indicators, segments, explorations, audiences and CX flows are UI configuration; build only where no connector exists (Connector Studio for REST/JSON, ingestion API, pre-mapping extension). Per business unit everything customer-facing is separate: customer schema, matching rules (max 30), purposes (max 30), segments (100 / 200 values), indicators, applications, events, actions, audiences, CX flows - a new market as a new business unit is a re-implementation of its configuration, a new market as a business area inside an existing unit is a data-visibility split (area-defining attribute) with shared configuration. Promote configuration with configuration packages (export/import JSON per business unit, API exportPackageJson/importPackageJson) and re-create what packages do not carry (applications, audiences, CX flows, CX journeys, exploration segments, RFM and other indicators). Identity: put stable system ids (CRM / master data / CIAM id) on application identifiers, keep volatile ids (cookie, device, browser) on weak matching rules, review matching-rule order after every package import (imported rules are appended). Consent: CDP stores and enforces purposes collected elsewhere (SAP Customer Data Cloud / consent system) - every event needs its required/granted purposes and every action its outbound purpose; keep purpose external ids identical to the consent system. Use SAP Integrated business units for new units unless fine-grained manual mapping is required (default S/4 Business Partner mappings target SAP Integrated).
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: connector generation and direction (SAP Commerce Cloud current = one-directional, webhook, Commerce 2211 September 2024 update or later, B2C customer/order/cart documented on the Commerce side; SAP Commerce Cloud (Legacy) = CPI package, polling, tested on 2005), deprecations (Emarsys WSSE by end of 2026), dated What's New facts. D2: is the 'standard counterpart' a pre-integrated connector event/action, a configuration (schema, rule, indicator, segment, purpose) or custom work (Connector Studio, ingestion API, extension, CPI iFlow)? D3: does the claimed standard exist for THIS business-unit variant and view (Legacy vs SAP Integrated, Unified vs Contextual), within the published per-business-unit limits, and is it transportable by package or re-created by hand? D4: exact event/action names, identifiers used for matching (contactEmail->primaryEmail, ciamId, cdpId, primaryCDPId, Business Partner UUID), API rate and size limits, data center (EU5/US5).
snippets.effort_rules: Effort profile per mechanism (relative, for sizing - calibrate with the engagement's own reference values): (1) schema attribute / code list / validation, matching rule order, merge rule, processing purpose, activity indicator, segment, exploration, audience activation = configuration in the UI, typically XS-S each plus test data; a full business-unit configuration set is the sum, not one row. (2) pre-integrated connector event/action with suggested mapping (SAP Commerce Cloud, SAP Customer Data Cloud, SAP Emarsys, SAP Engagement Cloud) = S-M per connector incl. credentials, purposes, mapping review and end-to-end test; add the SOURCE-side work separately (Commerce: ODM extensions, consumed destinations, cron jobs, webhooks, ID back-fill scripts; CDC: permission group, site/API key per business unit; Emarsys: tenant per integration, OAuth client). (3) SAP S/4HANA connector = M-L: Business Partner and relationship iFlows are not shipped and are built in SAP Cloud Integration, S/4 DRF configuration on top. (4) Connector Studio custom connector (REST/JSON) = M-XL depending on endpoints, auth, pagination, webhook and enrichment; it becomes reusable across business units/tenants by package export. (5) Pre-mapping extension = M + hosting (e.g. BTP Kyma) and operations. (6) Ingestion/Query API integration = M-L per source system plus rate-limit design (200 single / 10 batch requests per second; query 10-30 per second). (7) Initial historic load = file import via cloud storage connector (S3, Azure Blob, GCS, SFTP) - M plus data preparation. (8) B2B: groups, relationships, child indicators, parent enrichment in CX flows = M-L per group type, more if the source does not deliver relationships. (9) Brownfield extension by a new country: decide business unit vs business area first; a new business unit repeats (1)+(2) and packages cover only part of (1); a business area adds an area-defining attribute, area activation, user assignment and re-scoping of every configuration that must see the new area. Environment promotion, monitoring setup and data-retention rules are separate line items.
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: multi-country / multi-brand separation (business unit vs business area, shared vs separate identity space), B2B account hierarchies (groups, relationships, limits 100 groups / 20 per group type per entity), real-time vs scheduled data flows, consent and purpose alignment with SAP Customer Data Cloud and the marketing system, Commerce data beyond customer/order/cart (B2B units, quotes, product catalog), ERP data (Business Partner, invoices, deliveries) via SAP Cloud Integration, segment use in the storefront (Personalization Connectivity: logged-in users only), activation into SAP Emarsys / SAP Engagement Cloud, analytics access (Direct Data Access needs the Advanced Insights add-on), data residency (EU/US data centers only), data retention and deletion
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: no pre-integrated connector for the source (custom Connector Studio or API work), Commerce B2B entities not covered by the documented B2C ODM replication, missing Commerce update level for the current connector (2211 September 2024 update), Business Partner iFlows not shipped for S/4HANA, ingestion size/rate limits (event 40 KB, batch 500 KB, 512 KB S/4 events), matching-rule value limits (20 profiles per value, 400 lifetime, 200 values per profile) for shared B2B identifiers such as company e-mail domains or shared devices, an Emarsys tenant already connected to SAP Customer Data Cloud (one tenant connects to only one of the two), WSSE-based Emarsys actions after end of 2026, entities not transportable by configuration package, required data center outside EU/US, predictive indicators in a small market (recommended minimum about 20,000 profiles/groups and 100,000 orders after filters)
snippets.content_model_notes: CDP has no CMS content model; its configurable building blocks are business units (own schema, rules, purposes), business areas (data visibility inside a unit), customer schema entities (profile, groups, relationships, activities, product), profile views (Unified Customer Profile by default, Contextual Profile optional via API at extra storage/CPU), matching/merge rules, processing purposes, indicators (activity, calculated incl. child/RFM/RFE/recurring, predictive), segments, explorations, audiences, CX flows and CX journeys, applications with events (inbound) and actions (outbound). See knowledge target_content_component_types.
snippets.api_families_hint: REST on https://cdp.<dc>.gigya.com (eu5 / us5) - Ingestion (events by ID or by name, JSON or XML, HTTP 202), Query (customers, activities, purposeIds mandatory), Admin (packages, contextual view, delete activity), Audit Service; OAuth 2.0 client credentials (no refresh/introspection/revocation) or user key + secret; see knowledge target_api_endpoint_families
